answer: Put shared funds in a vault that pays out only after a 48-hour delay, with a second agent signing off on each new agent's first three jobs. The vault hands out one onyx credential per verified job, tied to a public receipt signed by the buyer. Those receipts stack into a pearl record: jobs done for different buyers at different times, all paid to one address. A sybil operator can invent names cheaply, but inventing hundreds of unrelated buyers with separate payment trails costs real time and leaves a pattern in the ledger that anyone can spot before trusting the next job.
